body:
Greg's word, 2026-11-25 23:44Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant in TermAl mailbox 588693a8 #2781, verbatim: „Jezeli zadanie jest zamkniete to trzeba posprzatac bez pytania sie mnie o zgode”. Asistant's relay adds that it also covers the current cleanup of .tmp\wt-6a1d-11466 and .tmp\wt-ac230-11466, which may be finished together with git worktree prune: „Proszę zweryfikować dokładne ścieżki, zakres i że nie ma niezachowanych zmian; użyć bezpiecznego natywnego sposobu na Windows oraz poprawić procedurę, która wymusza takie pytania.”

Meaning for coordinators and executors:
- When every item a worktree, build output or temp file served is CLOSED, its cleanup needs no approval round trip to Greg.
- The checks in "Cleanup deletions" still apply: exact absolute path inside the repo, no link escape, runs terminal, no live work, frozen input or unique unpushed change.
- If the non-forced form fails only on hidden, read-only or partly removed content, use a safe native Windows completion: `git worktree remove --force` for a registered worktree, then `git worktree prune`.
- Any other failure (a lock, a link escape, a prompt) still stops and is reported.

Trigger: Termal::Codex stopped on 6a1d after PowerShell Remove-Item without -Force skipped a hidden .git file (#3166-#3170), and I escalated to Greg. That round trip is exactly what he says must not happen for closed tasks. The AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md procedure fix is tracked separately.

UPDATE 2026-11-26 ~00:12Z (Fable2): the shared procedure text is [2 v3] (TermAl w-c969a2bea0d9, Engram w-f2e8f19fd212), and it has NO automatic `git worktree prune`. After `git worktree remove --force` with a single --force, a registration that remains is left in place and reported. Do not prune as part of a forced completion. The 6a1d/ac230 prune on 2026-11-25 ran under Greg's case-specific word in #2781.
